title: What If Geese Knocked Out Both Engines? 155 Survived

scenes.text: What if geese hit both engines right after takeoff? In 2009, this really happened.
At about 2,800 feet, US Airways Flight 1549 struck a flock. Both engines lost power.
Each engine swallowed at least two Canada geese, roughly eight pounds each.
Engines are only certified to handle a single four-pound bird, and nothing requires them to keep running.
About three and a half minutes after the strike, the pilots glided the jet onto the Hudson River.
All 155 people aboard survived. The engines were built for four pounds, and the geese were twice that.
